thread:
kai: Found these fortune cookies in the breakroom: each one had a tiny semver inside instead of a proverb :thinking_face:

kai: one said: `You will soon encounter minor changes; patch them gently.` I feel personally attacked

nora: please tell me one said `breaking changes are opportunities` so I can scream internally

sam: the compiler horoscope for today:
```text
Aries: avoid global state. Mercury in retrograde may rebind your callbacks.
Taurus: semver advice - bump patch often, panic rarely.
```

kai: also saw a cookie with YAML advice: `always mind your indentation or the parser will whisper`

build-bot: ci-notify: lint-check failed on `breakroom/notes.yaml` - unexpected token at line 3 (colon placement)

nora: classic. who let the YAML gremlin near the cookie jar?

sam: proposing a new kitchen rule: fortune-cookie-versioning. If the cookie says `1.0`, it's ceremonial only

kai: side quest: design a tiny CLI that prints a random semver fortune e.g. `cookie --fortune` -> "v0.2.0: try adding more snacks"

build-bot: deploy-bot: note - do not commit fortune-cookie outputs to repo. They cause mysterious merge conflicts.

nora: can we raffle a sticker pack: "I survived the YAML gremlin"? low-cost morale booster

snack-bot: Reminder: cookie refill scheduled at 15:00 :cookie: (third round dedicated to minor-version optimists)

sam: idea: hold a micro-hack to implement semver-based snacks. patch -> chips, minor -> cookies, major -> full breakfast

kai: I will prototype a `snackfile.yaml` and intentionally misindent one line for authenticity

nora: please DON'T. My heart can't take real lint errors in the wild

build-bot: friendly reminder: linting is a lifestyle, not a suggestion. Semver fortunes are not exempt.

sam: tl;dr: bring cookies, write a silly CLI, and don't let the YAML gremlin near the YAML cat's nap spot :cat_nap:
